note: Figures are quoted from the cited publications. Percentages in the chart are shares of HTML requests or crawler traffic as defined by each source; they are not directly comparable across sources.

facts.text: AI "user action" fetches (someone asking an assistant to read a page) grew more than 15× during 2025, driven by ChatGPT-User.
GPTBot accounted for roughly 7.5% of all verified-bot traffic; GPTBot, ClaudeBot and CCBot were the user agents most often fully disallowed in robots.txt.
Anthropic's crawl-to-refer ratio reached about 70,900 pages crawled per referral in June 2025, and as much as 500,000:1 later in the year; Mistral's was below 1:1.
facts.source: Cloudflare, Crawl before the fall of referrals

facts.text: About 14% of the top 10,000 domains carry AI-specific robots.txt directives.

As reported by Vercel: in one month GPTBot made 569 million requests and Claude 370 million against Googlebot's 4.5 billion; over a third of AI-crawler requests hit 404 pages, and neither crawler executes JavaScript.
facts.source: Vercel, The rise of the AI crawler

facts.text: As reported by the Wikimedia Foundation: bots generate about 65% of the most expensive traffic while making up roughly 35% of pageviews, and multimedia bandwidth rose 50% since January 2024, attributed to AI scrapers.
facts.source: Wikimedia Diff, How crawlers impact the operations of the Wikimedia projects

facts.text: As reported by Fastly: crawlers make up about 80% of AI-bot traffic, and 98% of on-demand fetcher traffic comes from OpenAI.
As reported by TollBit: the ratio of AI-bot visits to human visits moved from about 1:200 in early 2025 to about 1:31 by the end of the year, and retrieval bots now out-scrape training crawlers.
